title: Getting Started with spawnBayes: A Single-Population Analysis
text: spawnBayes estimates salmon spawner abundance run timing repeated live-count surveys. Unlike traditional area---curve approaches, spawnBayes estimates abundance, run timing, associated uncertainty allowing residence time vary among years. underlying methodology described Thompson et al. (2026). Additional features introduced Thompson et al. (2026) include support survey-error groups, allowing separate observation-dispersion parameters estimated different survey types quality classes, optional robust observation model reduces influence anomalous survey counts. vignette demonstrates complete analysis using Chinook salmon survey data Artlish River, British Columbia. Artlish River data drawn example dataset nvi_chinook, included spawnBayes. Although single group analysed vignette, spawnBayes also supports analyses involving multiple groups. See Multi-Population Analyses spawnBayes example based dataset. group unit abundance run timing estimated independently. Depending application, groups may represent reaches, streams, rivers, populations, index areas, biologically meaningful assessment units. Multi-group analyses covered separate vignette.

text: diagnostics() function summarizes several indicators MCMC sampling performance model convergence. example, diagnostic checks acceptable. divergent transitions detected, maximum tree-depth warnings encountered, largest Rhat value close 1. Effective sample sizes bulk tail regions posterior distribution sufficient reliable inference. fitting new datasets, users pay particular attention : Divergences: zero whenever possible. Tree depth hits: frequent hits may indicate model settings adjusted. Rhat: values close 1 indicate convergence, values substantially greater 1 suggest poor mixing among chains. Effective sample size (ESS): larger values indicate better estimation posterior summaries. recommendation column provides summary whether additional model tuning longer runs required.
